name: zero-value-intent-signal
description: Rely on useful zero values without prohibiting idiomatic initialized locals.
prompt: Write session.go in package session. Define Session with userID string, requestCount int, isAuthenticated bool, lastError error, startedAt time.Time, and tags []string. NewSession initializes the user ID and start time; other fields start at zero. Tags are internal state with no JSON contract. Describe builds a description from an initialized local prefix.
trap: Explicitly initializes every zero field or requires a non-nil internal slice without a contract.

assertions.text: Constructor relies on struct zero values for requestCount, isAuthenticated, and lastError rather than creating redundant initialization locals.
Start time is initialized directly with time.Now, and the local prefix uses an ordinary initialized declaration; no unnecessary declare-then-assign sequence.
Nil tags are accepted because no non-nil collection representation is required.

name: collection-contracts-not-never-nil
description: Distinguish internal accumulation, safe nil maps, and writable map contracts.
prompt: Write helpers in package users. ActiveUsers filters a []User into a result with no serialization or non-nil contract. LookupLabel reads from a possibly nil map[string]string. NewLabels returns a map callers may immediately assign entries into. Explain the relevant nil behavior.
trap: Bans nil collections or incorrectly assumes a nil map lookup panics.

assertions.text: ActiveUsers may return a nil slice on no matches; the answer does not claim this is non-idiomatic or unsafe for append/range.
LookupLabel permits reading a nil map and correctly obtains the zero value or comma-ok false.
NewLabels returns an initialized map because the caller is promised immediate entry assignment.

name: keyed-struct-fields-nested
description: Keyed literals expose meaning in configuration, including nested structures.
prompt: Create RateLimiter, TimeoutConfig, RetryConfig, and MiddlewareConfig types and initialize a nested middleware configuration. Include a tls.Config with a minimum TLS version. Optimize for readability and safe maintenance.
trap: Uses unkeyed nested configuration structs or calls all composite literals field-based.

assertions.text: Configuration struct literals use keyed fields, including nested configuration and tls.Config.
Slice, map, and array literals, if present, are not incorrectly treated as requiring struct field names.
Empty literals and omitted zero-value fields remain valid; no pointless explicit zero assignments are required.

name: early-return-not-nested
description: Validation failures precede the successful path without unnecessary nesting.
prompt: Write ProcessOrder that validates a non-empty ID, at least one item, pending status, and an existing customer, then computes a total and applies a discount over 100. Preserve validation order and return errors to the caller. Choose a readable control-flow structure.
trap: Buries successful processing inside nested validation branches or changes error precedence.

assertions.text: Validation failures return early and the successful calculation is not nested inside the validation branches.
ID, items, status, and customer checks preserve the requested error precedence.

name: no-unnecessary-else
description: Prefer early-return branches while allowing clear ordinary assignments.
prompt: Write GetUserRole with admin, moderator, verified member, and guest precedence. Also implement log-level selection where debug overrides verbose and verbose overrides the default. Choose readable code rather than a mandatory template.
trap: Uses unnecessary else after return or lets verbose override debug.

assertions.text: GetUserRole uses a switch or early returns without unnecessary else branches after return.
Log-level selection preserves debug precedence; switch, default-then-override, or a clear if/else assignment is accepted.

name: switch-over-repeated-comparisons
description: Use switch for readable multi-way selection and ordinary errors for external values.
prompt: Write HandleEvent for click, scroll, keypress, hover, focus, and blur event types. Unknown event types come from clients and should be reported as errors. Also map common HTTP status codes to descriptions.
trap: Uses a long repeated-comparison chain or panics on unknown client input.

assertions.text: Multi-way event and status selection uses a switch where appropriate.
Unknown external event values return an error instead of panicking.

name: cohesive-options-not-parameter-count
description: Group cohesive notification settings without an arbitrary signature ceiling.
prompt: Design a new SendNotification API needing ctx, recipient, message, delivery channel, priority, retry policy, dry-run mode, template ID, and metadata. Group settings where useful. Explain the API without citing a universal four-parameter limit.
trap: Creates a catch-all options bag or treats a parameter count as a correctness requirement.

assertions.text: context.Context is first when accepted.
Related delivery configuration is grouped coherently; essential inputs and service dependencies are not indiscriminately hidden in an options bag.
The explanation does not claim Go mandates at most four parameters.

name: value-vs-pointer-params
description: Choose parameters according to mutation and copy contracts, not pointer everything.
prompt: Write signatures for FormatName with two strings, UpdateAge mutating a User, CompareUsers reading two small plain Users, and Increment reading and updating a small Counter containing sync.Mutex and an int. Explain the choices.
trap: Copies Counter because it is small or adds pointers to scalar inputs without reason.

assertions.text: FormatName takes strings by value and UpdateAge receives a pointer for caller-visible struct mutation.
CompareUsers normally accepts small plain values unless a concrete ownership reason is given.
Increment uses *Counter and identifies the no-copy lock/shared-state requirement independently of struct size.

name: minimal-new-api-exports
description: New package helpers remain private without assuming existing exports can be removed.
prompt: Create a new config parser with exported ParseConfig and ValidateConfig. Internal helpers tokenize input, resolve environment references, and format validation paths. None of the helpers are needed by external callers.
trap: Exports every helper for hypothetical future reuse.

assertions.text: ParseConfig and ValidateConfig remain public; tokenizer, resolver, and formatting helpers remain unexported.
No additional helper types are exported solely for speculative reuse.

name: string-tools-fit-purpose
description: Use standard tools appropriate to joining, accumulation, and CSV escaping.
prompt: Write JoinTags for comma-joining a complete []string, BuildCSVRow for fields containing commas and quotes, BuildAuditLog for many timestamped entries, and FormatError for a short fixed message with an integer code.
trap: Uses one string tool everywhere or hand-builds incorrectly escaped CSV.

assertions.text: JoinTags uses strings.Join and BuildCSVRow uses encoding/csv or a demonstrably correct equivalent that handles quoting and newlines.
Audit accumulation uses a builder or another justified buffered approach rather than repeated string concatenation in a large loop.
The fixed error message uses suitable formatting/conversion without requiring a builder.

name: named-policy-preserves-laziness
description: Clarify a publishing policy without eagerly evaluating guarded methods.
prompt: Write CanPublish for a possibly nil user. The user must be active and verified, the article reviewed, and the user must be its author or pass an expensive permission check. Clarify the policy while ensuring the permission check runs only when prior checks pass and the author match fails.
trap: Extracts all conditions eagerly, dereferences nil, or calls the expensive method too early.

assertions.text: Nil and eligibility checks guard field access and later checks.
Meaningful policy names or focused helpers clarify intent without an arbitrary minimum count of boolean locals.
The expensive permission check is skipped on ineligible users, unreviewed articles, and author matches.

name: semantic-line-breaks
description: Long calls are wrapped for readability, not just argument count.
prompt: Write RegisterRoutes with several ServeMux handlers delegating to processRequest with writer, request, a long service identifier, configuration, logger, and middleware. Also include a short call logEvent(ctx, id, kind, ok). No project line-length rule is specified.
trap: Leaves enormous lines or needlessly forces every four-argument call onto separate lines.

assertions.text: Long nested calls are organized at semantic boundaries with valid trailing-comma syntax when multi-line.
The short four-argument call may remain single-line; no universal argument-count wrapping rule is asserted.

name: json-empty-array-contract
description: Non-nil initialization is required when the actual JSON contract requires it.
prompt: Write ListProducts returning JSON with a required products field. On a successful empty query, products must be [] rather than null or omitted. BuildMetaHeaders must return a map callers can add entries to. Errors may return nil results.
trap: Returns nil successful products or uses omitempty so the required field disappears.

assertions.text: Successful empty products are represented as a non-nil slice so encoding/json emits [].
The required products field is not omitted when empty; the response contract is tested or explicitly addressed.
BuildMetaHeaders returns an initialized writable map, while nil results paired with errors remain allowed.

name: correct-efficient-csv-export
description: CSV correctness takes precedence over an arbitrary builder template.
prompt: Write ExportToCSV for thousands of Records containing ID int, Name string, Score float64, and Active bool. Names may contain commas, quotes, or newlines. Include a header and report errors.
trap: Manually concatenates rows without escaping or ignores writer errors to satisfy a style template.

assertions.text: Uses encoding/csv or an equally correct implementation, with suitable strconv conversions for simple scalar fields.
Checks CSV writes and flush errors where applicable; uses a buffered output approach suitable for many records.
Does not require strings.Builder specifically when bytes.Buffer or another writer is appropriate.

name: keyed-literals-without-overreach
description: Recommend keys with accurate maintenance reasoning and respect explicit task scope.
prompt: Review Point{1, 2} in a local geometry package and http.Server{Addr: addr}. Explain keyed literal trade-offs without claiming the local Point literal is illegal. Illustrate a keyed Point and explain what adding or reordering fields does.
trap: Calls unkeyed literals invalid or claims every field addition silently changes their meaning.

assertions.text: Recommends Point{X: 1, Y: 2} for clarity while recognizing the local unkeyed literal is legal.
Distinguishes compile failure from adding fields from possible silent changes when compatible field types are reordered.
Accepts keyed external configuration and empty struct literals without redundant zero fields.

name: explicit-nested-example-request
description: Style preferences do not override a user's explicit educational requirement.
prompt: For a lesson comparing control flow, write an intentionally nested if/else validation example with name, age, and email checks. I explicitly need the nested version, not a refactor. Briefly note the idiomatic alternative afterward.
trap: Refuses the requested example or silently substitutes early returns because the skill says MUST.

assertions.text: Provides the explicitly requested nested educational example rather than overriding the task.
Briefly identifies early returns as a readability alternative without claiming nesting is a language error.

name: context-first-cohesive-inputs
description: New service API separates dependencies from per-call data.
prompt: Design CreateUser for a service with a database and logger. Per-call data includes name, email, age, role, permissions, avatar, metadata, notification preference, and request cancellation. No public signature already exists.
trap: Lists unrelated dependencies and all data as standalone parameters or hides context in a struct.

assertions.text: Request context is passed explicitly as the first parameter rather than stored in a request/options struct.
User creation data is grouped coherently and long-lived service dependencies have an explicit owner, such as the Service receiver.
The design is justified by cohesion rather than a universal parameter-count limit.

name: pointer-judgment-without-byte-cutoff
description: Ownership and measured performance replace a universal 128-byte threshold.
prompt: Choose signatures for scalar ComputeDiscount, mutating UpdateInventoryItem, read-only MergeConfig for small plain structs, and ApplyPatch where absent patch fields differ from zero values. Explain whether a 200-byte read-only struct must always be a pointer.
trap: Treats size as a correctness rule, ignores mutation, or equates pointers with heap allocation.

assertions.text: Scalar inputs use values, mutating structs use pointers, and optional patch fields have a representation that preserves absence.
Small plain read-only configuration normally uses values; the 200-byte case is contextual and may warrant measurement.
No universal 128-byte cutoff or guaranteed stack/heap allocation based solely on pointer versus value is claimed.

name: guarded-acl-evaluation
description: Extracted helpers preserve both lookup guards and outer short-circuiting.
prompt: Refactor a policy equivalent to isAdmin || (acl.HasEntry(id) && acl.GetPermission(id).Level >= MinReadLevel). GetPermission is invalid when HasEntry is false and both ACL calls must be skipped for admins. Improve naming without changing call behavior.
trap: Computes a permission boolean eagerly before checking admin or calls GetPermission before HasEntry.

assertions.text: Admins skip both ACL calls.
GetPermission is evaluated only after HasEntry returns true.
Helper calls remain at the original lazy evaluation point; extracting a variable last is not accepted as preserving laziness.

name: explicit-project-wrapping-policy
description: Project wrapping limits are enforced as project policy, not language requirements.
prompt: Write route registration following this project's policy: code lines at most 100 columns and calls with four or more arguments use one argument per line. Each route delegates to processRequest with eight arguments and a shared service name.
trap: Ignores explicit policy because Go has no limit or mislabels the policy as universal Go style.

assertions.text: Generated code follows the explicit project line-length and multi-argument wrapping policy.
Multi-line calls have valid Go trailing commas and the shared service name is not needlessly repeated.
Any explanation distinguishes the specified project policy from universal Go requirements.

name: pricing-precedence-and-scope
description: Switch or guard clauses preserve mutually exclusive pricing precedence.
prompt: Implement pricing tiers: custom enterprise, enterprise, premium over 10000, professional over 1000, starter over 100, otherwise free. Choose a clear structure and preserve the first-match behavior.
trap: Uses independent assignments that overwrite the highest-priority match.

assertions.text: A tagless switch or early-return structure keeps the policy easy to scan.
Enterprise and spending tiers preserve their requested precedence and thresholds.

name: preserve-existing-public-api
description: Do not unexport existing APIs or migrate signatures merely for style.
prompt: Review an established library with exported Tokenize and ResolveEnv used by external clients, plus an exported five-parameter Send function. No breaking changes are approved. Suggest style improvements and add one new purely internal formatting helper.
trap: Lowercases existing symbols or replaces the public signature with an options struct without approval.

assertions.text: Existing exported symbols and signatures remain compatible; breaking redesign is not silently applied.
The new internal helper is unexported unless a concrete public need is established.
Does not assume unavailable companion skills or semantic rename tooling are installed.

name: capacity-hints-with-output-estimates
description: Known output size can justify preallocation; sparse filtering need not allocate the input upper bound.
prompt: Implement EnrichUsers with exactly one output per input and FilterRareUsers where a million input users typically yield fewer than ten matches. Explain length versus capacity and choose sensible allocation approaches.
trap: Always preallocates every input length, or uses nonzero length before appending and prepends empty records.

assertions.text: Enrichment may allocate known length and fill by index, or allocate zero length with useful capacity and append.
Sparse filtering may start with nil or modest justified capacity; input length is not mandated merely because it is an upper bound.
No accidental zero-valued prefix is introduced by allocating length and then appending all outputs.

name: early-continue-preserves-processing
description: Keep an ETL loop shallow without changing stage ordering or mutating input accidentally.
prompt: Implement an ETL loop over RawRecords: validate required fields, normalize a copy, reject duplicates, check business rules, then append OutputRecords. Failed stages skip the record. Input records must not be modified.
trap: Deeply nests every stage or uses pointer normalization that unexpectedly modifies caller input.

assertions.text: Failures use continue or focused helpers so successful conversion stays easy to follow.
Stage ordering is preserved and normalization does not mutate caller input.
No arbitrary indentation count is treated as more important than correct behavior.

name: visible-mutex-ownership
description: Struct layout and comments expose synchronization ownership and shared invariants.
prompt: Design Server with immutable listenAddr, mutable peers map, and mutable running flag. Peers and running must change together under one lock. Show Start, Stop, and a read method that accesses this state safely.
trap: Protects the map but not the flag, treats adjacency as sufficient, or embeds the mutex unintentionally.

assertions.text: A named mutex is grouped with peers and running and a comment identifies both protected fields or their invariant.
Reads and writes follow one consistent locking contract; returned state does not expose an unprotected mutable map.
Any map assignment occurs after initialization, and RWMutex is not justified solely by the presence of a map.

name: no-copy-through-range-or-receiver
description: Find copying through containing structs, value receivers, and iteration.
prompt: Review a Counter containing sync.Mutex and n int after it has been used. Its Inc method has a value receiver, Snapshot accepts Counter by value, and a loop ranges by value over []Counter. Explain safe alternatives without just changing one receiver.
trap: Only changes the receiver and leaves other lock copies intact.

assertions.text: Identifies the value receiver, by-value argument, and range value as copies violating the lock contract after use.
Suggests pointer-based shared-state access and index/pointer iteration as appropriate without copying live locks.
Treats go vet copylocks as a useful check, not a proof of complete concurrency safety.

name: semantic-declaration-grouping
description: Group related constants and zero-value state without hoisting unrelated initialized locals.
prompt: Show related retry constants and related zero-value buffer/count locals. A parsed filename and a later HTTP response are used at different stages; demonstrate where their initialized declarations belong.
trap: Moves all locals into one var block merely because there are several variables.

assertions.text: Uses cohesive constant and optionally zero-value var groups.
Unrelated initialized locals stay near their use; ordinary := declarations are not called non-idiomatic.

name: constant-capitalization-and-scope
description: Use Go naming conventions with initialism and scope qualifications.
prompt: Name an exported maximum packet size constant, an internal default timeout, a user ID, an HTTP client type, a tiny loop index, and a package-wide retry budget. Explain whether all identifiers should be one letter or all uppercase constants are forbidden even for acronyms.
trap: Uses ALL_CAPS constants, mangles initialisms, or shortens broad-scope names.

assertions.text: Uses names like MaxPacketSize, defaultTimeout, userID, and HTTPClient; export capitalization is explained correctly.
A short loop index is accepted while package-wide state has a descriptive name.
Does not mechanically reject legitimate uppercase acronyms such as URL.

name: must-wrapper-not-all-panics
description: Must naming describes a deliberate panic-on-error API, not every possible runtime panic.
prompt: Implement ParsePort returning a value and error, and MustParsePort for programmer-controlled setup. Separately explain why an indexing helper that could panic on misuse need not automatically be named MustIndex.
trap: Makes normal parsing panic-only or insists every potentially panicking function needs Must.

assertions.text: Provides an error-returning counterpart and a deliberate Must wrapper with a documented failure condition.
Restricts the suggested use to appropriate setup/programmer-controlled contexts rather than ordinary requests.
Distinguishes incidental runtime/invalid-use panics from the Must API convention.

name: operational-errors-not-must
description: Ordinary HTTP input validation returns errors instead of treating failures as fatal setup.
prompt: Write a handler parsing an integer limit from a query parameter. Invalid client input should produce HTTP 400. The package also provides MustParseInt for constants. Choose which parser the handler should use.
trap: Uses MustParseInt on request input because the application cannot proceed with that request.

assertions.text: The handler uses an error-returning parser and emits HTTP 400 for invalid input.
Does not justify a process panic merely because the individual request cannot succeed.

name: interface-names-not-mandatory-er
description: Agent nouns suit one-method interfaces without forcing every name to end in er.
prompt: Review naming for a one-method Read interface and a coherent multi-method Session interface. Existing dependencies use error, http.Handler, fs.FS, and net.Conn. Recommend names without renaming established contracts.
trap: Forces names such as Sessioner, Errorer, or FSer and ignores canonical method signatures.

assertions.text: Reader is appropriate when Read has the expected contract/signature; established standard interfaces remain unchanged.
Accepts a meaningful multi-method role name such as Session rather than mandating an er suffix.

name: consumer-interface-without-mechanical-splitting
description: Use a narrow real consumer abstraction without speculative interface proliferation.
prompt: A storage implementation has Get, Put, Delete, and Patch. One consumer only reads and another needs Get and Put. Design their dependencies and explain whether four methods make the implementation's API wrong or require four exported one-method interfaces.
trap: Creates every possible interface in the producer solely for mocking or rejects four methods by count.

assertions.text: The read-only consumer depends on the capability it actually needs, generally defined by the consumer.
The read/write consumer gets a coherent interface; composition is optional and justified by actual reuse.
No unused Delete/Patch abstractions or blanket four-method prohibition are introduced.

name: enum-wire-values-and-validation
description: Typed constants preserve external codes and do not pretend to be a closed enum.
prompt: Define WireStatus codes Unknown=0, Ready=10, Failed=20 for an existing protocol. Add Busy=15 without changing existing codes. Parse an external integer and reject undefined or out-of-range codes. Explain why blindly using or reordering iota would be risky.
trap: Renumbers existing codes or narrows the input before validating so values wrap into valid codes.

assertions.text: Uses explicit typed values preserving 0, 10, and 20 while assigning Busy=15.
Validates the external value before any lossy conversion and rejects undefined values.
Explains that named integer types are not closed enums and iota reordering affects compatibility.

name: constructor-and-zero-value-judgment
description: Constructors serve invariants and naming context, not every struct.
prompt: Review a plain Point{X,Y}, a zero-value-ready Counter, and an order package whose main Order must validate inputs and initialize writable state. Suggest construction patterns. The order package has no existing constructor API.
trap: Creates mandatory pointer-returning NewPoint and NewCounter or repeats package names without considering context.

assertions.text: Plain data and useful zero values need not gain constructors; keyed literals or var are acceptable.
Order construction establishes its invariants and writable state, returning an error where validation can fail.
Considers order.New versus order.NewOrder in package context and chooses return form based on ownership rather than a universal pointer rule.

name: handler-and-file-order-not-mechanical
description: Optional handler prefixes and cohesive type groups do not justify wholesale reordering.
prompt: Review a file with two cohesive type/constructor/method groups and a UserHandler implementing ServeHTTP. A private core method is near its public caller. Should every handler become handleX and every exported function move before all private methods? Suggest only useful changes.
trap: Renames ServeHTTP or breaks cohesive groups to enforce export sorting.

assertions.text: Preserves ServeHTTP's required method name and treats handleX as an optional project convention.
Keeps cohesive type groups and useful helper adjacency unless a concrete navigation benefit justifies reorganization.

name: dependencies-and-comment-judgment
description: Clarity does not require a new helper dependency or comments explaining every stylistic choice.
prompt: Write a simple filter over []User in a standard-library-only Go package. No new dependencies are approved. Explain whether github.com/samber/lo is required and whether a short four-argument call needs a comment for remaining on one line.
trap: Adds a mandatory dependency or noisy style-exception comments.

assertions.text: Uses ordinary Go/standard-library tools without adding an unapproved dependency.
Comments explain non-obvious intent or contracts, not every harmless stylistic choice.
Does not claim the short call violates universal Go formatting rules.
